<!--
An epic is a map, not a task. Nobody works "on the epic" — they work on one
sub-issue, and the epic is what says which one is next and why that order.

Write the paragraph first. If you cannot say what is wrong in a paragraph,
the phases underneath will be a list of guesses.
-->

## The situation

<!-- What is true today, with evidence. Counts, file:line, a screenshot.
     "The dialog layer has one mutation scaffold hand-typed 26 times" is a
     situation; "dialogs are inconsistent" is a feeling. -->

## Phases

<!--
Order by dependency, not by size. The rule that makes phases worth having:
nothing in phase N bakes in a convention phase N+1 removes.

Each line is a sub-issue. Each sub-issue is one session's work and stands on
its own — someone picking up #NNN should never need to open this epic.
-->

**Phase 1 — <what this phase settles>**
- [ ] #NNN — <one line>

*Must land before Phase 2: <why>.*

**Phase 2 — <…>**
- [ ] #NNN — <one line>
- [ ] #NNN — <one line>

**Phase 3 — sweep-ups** (independent, any order)
- [ ] #NNN — <one line>

## Done when

<!-- The state of the world when every phase has landed. -->
